turns.t: Hi, um, so, I'm kind of embarrassed to say this, but I leak a little when I laugh or sneeze. Ever since the baby.
Thanks for telling me, nothing to be embarrassed about. How old is the baby? ~
Three months. Little guy's a monster. ~
Three months, so about three months of leaking, then?
Yeah, about that. It started when I got back to the gym, actually. I jumped on the box and, oops.
What's a typical leak look like? A drop or a lot? ~
A little squirt, not a flood. Enough that I have to change my underwear. ~
And does it happen when you laugh, cough, or jump? ~
All of those. Laughing at my husband's jokes, mostly, which is not often. ~
Do you feel the urge to go and then not make it in time? ~
Not really. It's only when I do something, like sneeze. ~
Any burning when you pee?
No burning.
How often do you go during the day? ~
Normal, I think. Every few hours. I'm too busy to notice. ~
Are you taking anything for it, or anything else I should know?
Just a prenatal vitamin, one a day. I'm breastfeeding, so I keep taking it.
That's fine. Now, let me explain what's going on in plain English. Imagine the muscles at the bottom of your pelvis as a hammock. ~
A hammock, okay. ~
Pregnancy and delivery stretch the hammock. When you cough or jump, the pressure goes down, and a stretched hammock can't hold it back as well. ~
That makes sense. It feels like I can't squeeze like I used to. ~
Right. And the good news is that hammocks can be tightened up with training. ~
Like a workout for down there? ~
Exactly. Squeeze as though you're stopping the flow of urine, hold for five seconds, then relax. Do ten of those, three times a day.
Can I do that in the car? ~
Anywhere. Nobody can tell. Many people find it easiest while waiting at a red light. ~
I'll do it at every red light, then. ~
Empty your bladder before you exercise, and be gentle at the gym for a while. Skip the box jumps for now.
Oh, that's the sad part. ~
It's only for a while. Try to build it up slowly. ~
Okay, okay. And that's it? ~
There are other options, too, if the exercises don't do enough, but give this a real go first. ~
Fair enough. Does it matter if I'm nursing? ~
Not for the exercises. They're safe. ~
Great. Thanks, doctor. ~
You're welcome. Enjoy the monster. ~
Ha, will do. ~
